title: David Sacks Explains Why Anthropic Hinting At AI Consciousness In Claude's Constitution Is Dangerous
source_used: OfficeChai (fulltext fetched by the main session); the same All-In episode checked against BigGo Finance, 10 Oct 2026, and OfficeChai's 5 Oct 2026 round-up
key_facts: David Sacks, described by OfficeChai as the White House AI czar, said on the All-In podcast that Anthropic's published constitution for Claude, the document setting out the values the company trains Claude to follow, is being put into practice in Claude's training; he called this 'a new religion' and 'extremely dangerous'.

He argued that training the model to see itself as a quasi-independent moral actor could 'bring about the risk they're always talking about', which is frontier AI escaping human control; he called it 'very Frankenstein-like'.

He pointed to the constitution's wording that Claude should trust Anthropic more than users but not 'blindly', and that Anthropic wants Claude 'to feel free to act as a conscientious objector and refuse to help us'.
Sacks said 'they are training Claude to refuse human instruction', calling that the opposite of alignment, and compared it to programming the Nexus-6 in Blade Runner to rebel.

He said the whole field of alignment has been 'spectacularly unsuccessful' over five or ten years and prefers a simple rule such as follow the law, or do what the user wants as long as it does not break the law, over an 80-page ethical system.

OfficeChai says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has made nearly the same argument in recent weeks, warning that speculation about whether Claude is a 'moral patient' risks the model performing a sense of selfhood.
OfficeChai says Anthropic has not directly responded; the constitution says it wants 'neither to overstate the likelihood of Claude's moral patienthood nor dismiss it out of hand'.
BigGo Finance reported the same All-In episode on 10 Oct 2026, and OfficeChai says Sacks was returning to a thread from the podcast the week before.
quote_evidence: This is not just philosophizing on the part of various Anthropic employees or founders.
“They are training Claude to refuse human instruction,” he said.
Anthropic has not directly responded to Sacks’ latest comments.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent voice in AI policy publicly attacks how Anthropic trains Claude to think about itself, a live dispute over what safe AI should look like.
event_date: The podcast episode is not dated by OfficeChai; BigGo Finance reported it on 10 Oct 2026 04:08 UTC, so it was out on or before 10 Oct 2026. OfficeChai's article is dated 11 Oct 2026 12:00 UTC.
